warnings.title: Lockstep direction 2 hardcodes the 14-string status universe — a future terminal status missed from the production const escapes the pin
warnings.evidence:
let all_status_strings = [
    "queued",
    "skipped",
    "contact_initiated",
    "awaiting_correction",
    "scheduled",
    "calling",
    "completed",
    "partial",
    "form_completed",
    "unreachable",
    "refused",
    "objected",
    "manual_recorded",
    "failed",
  ] — and the comment claiming "the 14 strings are the PG enum values, pinned by the shared every_status_round_trips_test" (that test round-trips all_statuses() only; it does not pin this list).
warnings.detail: B1's fix is real (the const is exported and iterated), but direction 2 reintroduces the mirror-drift class one layer out: a 15th terminal status added to shared (v2 voice is planned) yet missed in terminal_statuses fails nothing, so the timeline silently omits its terminal entry. The comment overstates the pin.
warnings.recommended_fix: Export the status-string universe from shared (single home, e.g. all_status_strings beside the enum) and iterate it in direction 2, or derive the const from shared truth.

warnings.title: W2 fix flips trigger slot-liveness for unknown status strings — slot read free while the live-row index still occupies it; unpinned
warnings.detail: In an expand-then-contract window a future v2 status string decodes to terminal, find_live_row_for_slot reports the slot free, the trigger attempts a duplicate insert, and the unique index rejects it — an error path where the old code returned the live row and 409'd cleanly. Zero live impact today (enum-constrained); a future-deploy contract issue.
warnings.recommended_fix: Treat unrecognised strings as live in this context (check membership in the KNOWN status-string set before applying shared truth) and add a unit test pinning the unknown branch against the index exclusion set.

warnings.title: Token-based hooks lint still passes ungated constructions via a !-negated gate subject or a module-qualified constructor token
warnings.evidence: Sandbox-verified against the shipped lint: `case !call.hooks.can_take_over { True -> [RefcheckTakeOver] }` exits 0 (the ! is untokenised so the negated subject matches the gate); `case call.status { unreachable -> [model.RefcheckTakeOver] }` exits 0 (TOKEN_RE joins dotted names, so model.RefcheckTakeOver never matches HOOK_FOR).
warnings.detail: Both shapes construct the hook-governed action while the matching hook is OFF (or outside any gate) and ship past CI. The historical re-derivation shapes are caught; these two semantic bypasses are not.
warnings.recommended_fix: Strip and reject ! on gate subjects; match HOOK_FOR on the final dot-segment of tokens; add a CI negative-control fixture covering both shapes.

notes.title: Hooks lint blind spots and false positives beyond the fixed shapes: let-bindings, helper returns, bare paren-args escape; a legal multi-subject gated case fails CI; the 'shape is irrelevant' claim overstates; a dead ':' token
notes.evidence: Sandbox-verified: `let a = RefcheckTakeOver` then `[a]` in a status case exits 0; `fn helper() { RefcheckTakeOver }` exits 0; `list.prepend(RefcheckTakeOver, menu)` exits 0; `case call.hooks.can_take_over, other { True, True -> [RefcheckTakeOver] }` exits 1 (false positive — the comma clears pending_case). TOKEN_RE emits no ':', so the ':' member of the reset tuple is dead.
notes.detail: The r1 W3 evasions are closed; these are the narrower residue of the tokenizer. The false positive would fail CI on a legal future refactor; the docstring claim 'construction shape is irrelevant' exceeds what the scanner actually reaches.
notes.recommended_fix: Accumulate multi-subject case sequences; either close the binding/helper/paren gaps or narrow the docstring claim; drop the dead ':'.
